title: Hardware fidelity, runtime and release maintenance
summary: Review eight material upstream changes spanning emulator fidelity, native runtime variants, completed disassembly status, compiler test architecture and release packaging.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas. New CPU metadata was added only where current primary diffs explicitly establish generated output architecture. No upstream project was compiled or executed by the tracker.

project.status: Active PS1 emulator/debugger: current source adds tested NTSC 480i DFE row suppression, SPU-mix WAV capture, safer legacy save-state GPU restoration and correct Lua breakpoint labels; independently unbuilt and unrun

identity.narrative: PCSX-Redux remains a general PlayStation emulator, debugger and development environment rather than a game-specific port.

classification.narrative: The reviewed changes materially extend hardware-fidelity and debugging facilities: the soft GPU now suppresses the displayed field's rows in NTSC 480i when DFE is clear, and Lua breakpoint labels are preserved.

source_cpu.narrative: The emulated PlayStation program architecture remains MIPS; this is source-platform provenance, not a host minimum.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed commits do not establish a fixed native host CPU target or minimum.

build.narrative: Upstream added a GPU regression test, SPU-mix capture to stereo 16-bit 44.1 kHz WAV, clean handling of write errors and the RIFF 4 GB limit, and a legacy save-state restoration correction.
build.limitations: The tracker reviewed source diffs but did not build, run, capture audio or reproduce the GPU regression.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum host CPU, RAM, operating system or GPU requirement is stated by these changes.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commits contain no development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: The work remains in the existing PCSX-Redux lineage and does not introduce a separate project.

runtime_profiles.name: OpenSWOS AGA WHDLoad package
runtime_profiles.notes: The project now builds and packages its own OpenSWOS.slave, launches SWOS2 directly without a Kickstart image or third-party slave, and was tested upstream under WHDLoad 19.2 in FS-UAE plus the project's harness. Exact physical CPU and RAM minima are not stated.

project.status: Active Amiga-derived C port; setup accepts floppy, HDF, LHA and ZIP sources and now packages a project-owned AGA WHDLoad slave without a Kickstart image or third-party slave; independently unbuilt and unrun

identity.narrative: OpenSWOS remains Ben Baker's Amiga-derived C port, distinct from the separately tracked Godot/C# recreation.

classification.narrative: The new setup recognizes multiple owned-source formats and the repository now contains its own WHDLoad slave and file/memory bridge, rather than merely repackaging a third-party slave.

source_cpu.narrative: The source/input lineage remains the Amiga m68k version of SWOS.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed Amiga Makefile assembles the native output and WHDLoad slave with explicit 68020 settings; this records the output architecture, not an independently measured hardware minimum.

build.narrative: Upstream reports that its own slave reaches the intro, menus and a match under WHDLoad 19.2 in FS-UAE, that Delete quits, and that the plain Workbench path still reaches the main menu. The setup now consumes floppy, HDF, LHA and ZIP sources and builds the package.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build, install or run these paths.

runtime_profiles.narrative: A bounded AGA WHDLoad variant is recorded from the upstream test. The project explicitly removes the prior Kickstart-image and third-party-slave requirements; CPU and RAM minima remain unstated.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5 as co-author.

relationships.narrative: The new WHDLoad packaging is a variant of this repository's existing OpenSWOS output, not a separate project.

project.status: Current ROM separates firmware initialization from |VH and upstream MAME coverage asserts no speech exchange occurs before |VH; physical LambdaSpeak hardware, native audio and minimum CPC requirements remain unverified

identity.narrative: Speaking Vector Head remains a Z80 CPC revival with separate disc and ROM builds plus optional LambdaSpeak speech integration.

classification.narrative: The ROM jump block now has a no-op firmware initialization entry and a separate |VH command, correcting the prior boot-time autorun while retaining an explicit user-start route.

source_cpu.narrative: The historical host/program architecture remains Z80.

target_cpu.narrative: The inspected ROM implementation remains native Z80 output.

build.narrative: The MAME regression regenerates and reads build symbols, counts LambdaSpeak exchanges before |VH, fails on any autorun and then checks the complete three-line intro buffer; upstream says the pre-fix ROM produces four premature exchanges.
build.limitations: The tracker did not assemble the ROM or execute MAME, physical hardware or audio output.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The changes establish ROM behavior but state no minimum CPC model, RAM or physical-card configuration.

ai.narrative: Both reviewed commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.

relationships.narrative: The corrected ROM remains a build variant within the existing project; the disc version is explicitly unchanged.

project.status: Active m68k-AmigaOS cross toolchain; current tests run 68000 boards on an emulated 68000 and add an explicit 68020/68881 FPU board; tracker did not reproduce the suite

identity.narrative: This remains the AmigaPorts cross-compiler/toolchain continuation for m68k AmigaOS output.

classification.narrative: The repository is retro-development tooling, not a recovered game or an emulator project.

source_cpu.narrative: There is no recovered historical binary input whose architecture should be recorded as source_cpu.

target_cpu.narrative: The toolchain emits m68k AmigaOS code. Current primary diffs distinguish 68000 test boards from a 68020 plus 68881 FPU board, supporting the output family without implying one universal minimum.

build.narrative: Upstream changed 68000 boards to execute on an emulated 68000 so misaligned accesses trap rather than being tolerated by a 68020, and added a CI-selected 68020/68881 FPU board because prior GCC tests used soft-float.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build the toolchain or run either test suite.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed emulator board RAM and stack settings are test-harness allocations, not minimum runtime requirements for software built by the toolchain.

ai.narrative: These two commits contain no development-AI attribution; that bounded absence does not establish non-use elsewhere.

relationships.narrative: The project remains the AmigaPorts continuation of the established m68k-AmigaOS GCC lineage.

project.status: Upstream now publishes the USA cartridge's annotated RGBDS assembly disassembly as a complete byte-exact reconstruction; optional semantic research and physical-hardware verification remain open

identity.narrative: This remains the BattleTanx Game Boy Color USA-ROM annotated assembly disassembly.

classification.narrative: The primary manifest now marks reconstruction status complete while explicitly distinguishing complete binary reconstruction from complete semantic recovery.

source_cpu.narrative: The recovered original program uses the Game Boy SM83 architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The RGBDS rebuild remains SM83 Game Boy Color output.

build.narrative: The current manifest and status document publish a complete byte-exact USA-cartridge reconstruction, and the repository check now requires status=complete.
build.limitations: The tracker did not obtain the original ROM, rebuild it or independently compare hashes; build flags remain unknown rather than converting the upstream claim into an independent test.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The completion update states no minimum physical hardware configuration beyond the existing GBC target, so no runtime profile is inferred.

ai.narrative: The reviewed completion commit contains no development-AI attribution; absence in this commit is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: The completion publication updates the existing disassembly; it does not establish a separate fork or successor.

runtime_profiles.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
runtime_profiles.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

runtime_profiles.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
runtime_profiles.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

runtime_profiles.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
runtime_profiles.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

runtime_profiles.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
runtime_profiles.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

runtime_profiles.name: Terra Strike: classic 68k AGA build
runtime_profiles.notes: The primary README explicitly states 68020+, AGA and AmigaOS 3.0+ for the classic build. No minimum RAM is stated; the tracker did not run it.

runtime_profiles.name: Terra Strike: PowerPC AmigaOS 4.1 build
runtime_profiles.notes: ARCH=ppc produces terra_strike_os4 with windowed/full-screen graphics and AHI audio. No physical PowerPC model or RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: Seven substantive original/homebrew game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PowerPC AmigaOS variants; Terra Strike now has a shared-gameplay AmigaOS 4.1 port; independently unbuilt

identity.narrative: Terra Strike is now a seventh substantive game subject in the existing multi-project homebrew collection, alongside the six previously reviewed anchors.

classification.narrative: Terra Strike is original Zarch/Carrier Command-style homebrew, not a reverse-engineered or binary-derived project; the new work ports the same source-level game to AmigaOS 4.1.

source_cpu.narrative: Terra Strike is a source-level original game, so no historical input-binary CPU is inferred.

target_cpu.narrative: The classic variant is explicitly 68020+ and the new AmigaOS 4.1 build is explicit PowerPC output; both families were already represented in the collection record.

build.narrative: The commit factors shared simulation/render/model/bridge code, adds ARCH=ppc output, a 25 Hz timer schedule, OS4 display paths and AHI plus software ProTracker audio.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile, launch, test controls, measure timing or verify audio on either architecture.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The classic Terra Strike README explicitly states 68020+, AGA and AmigaOS 3.0+. The PPC variant requires AmigaOS 4.1 but states no physical processor or RAM minimum.

ai.narrative: The commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5, consistent with the collection's prior affirmative AI evidence.

relationships.narrative: Terra Strike remains a subject within amiga_games and shares its AmigaBridge-oriented codebase; it is not split into a second repository record.

project.status: v1.13.2 adds a published Flynn 512Ke Telnet/Finger edition using talkip over LocalTalk without MacTCP or a networking INIT; independently unbuilt and unrun

runtime_profiles.name: Flynn 512Ke edition
runtime_profiles.notes: Published minimal-plus-Finger edition for a Macintosh 512Ke over LocalTalk, linked with talkip. Requires AppleTalk and a MacIP gateway; no MacTCP or networking INIT. The paired talkip release documentation states 128K ROM or later. No minimum CPU is inferred from the machine name.

identity.narrative: Flynn remains one native classic-Mac Telnet/Finger application; the 512Ke build is a fourth release edition, not a separate project.

classification.narrative: This remains substantial original homebrew/networking software rather than reverse-engineered code.

source_cpu.narrative: There is no recovered original binary whose architecture belongs in source_cpu.

target_cpu.narrative: The output remains native m68k Macintosh software; the reviewed release adds a 512Ke-specific build but does not justify a narrower CPU claim.

build.narrative: The new preset combines the minimal edition, Finger and talkip; release tooling pins talkip v0.1.0 and publishes dedicated 512Ke disk, BinHex and StuffIt artifacts.
build.limitations: The tracker did not cross-compile, install or run the release.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Primary documentation now establishes a concrete 512 KiB System 6 variant over LocalTalk with AppleTalk and a MacIP gateway, without MacTCP or a networking INIT. A CPU minimum is deliberately not inferred.

ai.narrative: The reviewed release commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5.

relationships.narrative: The 512Ke edition vendors/pins sibling project talkip as its network stack while Flynn and talkip remain separately tracked projects.

runtime_profiles.name: 512K Lite-client integration
runtime_profiles.os: System 6 with 128K ROM or later, LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway
runtime_profiles.notes: The v0.1.0 release packages five tools, the TalkIP Driver and AppleTalk On as an 800K HFS disk and StuffIt 1.5 archive. Primary documentation states a Macintosh with 128K ROM or later and 512 KiB RAM, but no minimum CPU is inferred from the machine family.

project.status: v0.1.0 released: packaged 512K System 6 TCP/IP tools and MacTCP-compatible driver for LocalTalk/MacIP, without MacTCP

identity.narrative: talkip remains a compact TCP/IP/MacIP stack, tools and MacTCP-compatible driver for early Macintosh systems over LocalTalk.

classification.narrative: The v0.1.0 packaging confirms substantive native networking software and developer tooling; it is original homebrew rather than recovered historical source.

source_cpu.narrative: No historical binary input is being reconstructed, so source_cpu remains empty.

target_cpu.narrative: The documented native output remains 68000 Macintosh software.

build.narrative: Release scripts now build a tagged checkout and package five tools, TalkIP Driver, AppleTalk On and documentation into an 800K HFS disk and StuffIt 1.5 archive.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build or inspect the binary artifacts.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The release Read Me explicitly requires 512 KiB RAM, 128K ROM or later, System 6, LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway. No CPU minimum is inferred beyond the separately evidenced 68000 output family.

ai.narrative: The release commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5.

relationships.narrative: The packaged stack remains a sibling dependency used by Flynn and Geomys; those applications retain separate records.
